text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which could position Australia to join the North American Free Trade Agreement trade bloc, embracing the US, Canada and America, Canada has offered Australia the chance to negotiate a free trade agreement, arguing that it could help business and encourage other countries into opening their markets. Page 1.

Australia's highest paid public company chief executive, Peter Bartels, whose A$2.87 million salary last year aroused controversy, was yesterday replaced at the head of Coles Myer Ltd, Australia's largest retailer, six months before the end of his contract. The position will go to Bartels' chief executive officer Dennis Eck. Page 1.

According to the latest survey by the Australian Institute of Company Directors and accounting house KPMG, Australian company directors are less likely to cite interest costs as a key factor affecting profits and of those who did cite interest rates as a factor, only five per cent expected them to move up and 70 per cent thought they would move down in the next quarter. Page 2.

Australian coal companies could face a price cut or a loss in market share after Chile agreed to give Canada preferential access under a new free-trade agreement, which will see the phase-out of an 11 per cent tariff. Australian companies must still pay the 11 per cent tariff, with BHP being the most heavily affected as it accounts for about A$30 million a year in exports to Chile. Page 4.

In a move which is intended to allow both parties to better prepare themselves ahead of the Federal Government's privatisation of Australian National and National Rail Corp, transport giant TNT and Toll Holdings have joined forces to capture a large portion of the A$500 million interstate rail linehaul market opened up by the sell-off of the national rail network. Page 19.

Following open warfare that has split two generations of the O'Brien family, who hold a 39 per cent stake in Defiance Mills Ltd through their company Defiance Holdings Ltd, Defiance Mills institutional shareholders yesterday dropped support for the O'Briens and voted independent director Corrs Chambers Westgarth partner John Story to the board of the struggling flour milling and baking group. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Coles Myer chairman Nobby Clark announced yesterday Peter Bartels' controversial four-year reign as chief executive of Australia's biggest retailer had come to an end after Bartels' employment agreement, which had been due to run until July next year, wasterminated six months early by mutual consent. Page 19.

Ansett International has suffered a setback to plans to expand overseas flights, with the International Air Services Commission - a Government statutory authority which allocates international air rights to airlines - rejecting its application under Section 54 of the LASC Act to take capacity away from Qantas Airways Ltd in order to operate daily flights between Australia and Hong Kong. Page 19.

The proposed A$1 billion-plus share market listing of the Ten Group Ltd has been undermined after CanWest Global Communications Inc - Ten's biggest shareholder - confirmed at the weekend it had bankrolled an "unassociated" Australian company to acquire abut 17 per cent of the network's ordinary shares - a move which indicates a deterioration in the already strained relations between Ten shareholders. Page 19.

The Transurban Holdings Ltd-led A$455 million capital raising for the A$1.8 billion Melbourne City Link project has won the Euromoney corporate finance magazine's Project Finance Deal of the Year award for 1996. The raising for the largest private sectorfunded road project in the world was assisted by Macquarie Bank's corporate finance department and while Macquarie Bank chairman Laurie Cox said the award would not help build the project, he said it would attract world-wide attention to Macquarie. Page 1.

In a surprise announcement, Korea's 13th largest company, the Halla Group , has signed a memorandum of understanding with Asia Iron Ltd's parent, Resources Equities Ltd, for a A$1 billion direct reduction iron project producing two million tonnes a year, bsed on a magnetite deposit at Mt Gibson, between Perth and Geraldton. Page 21.

After lobby groups yesterday mounted their final attempt to convince the Senate to amend proposed legislation to cut the research and development tax concession rate and abolish R&D tax syndication, the Senate Economics Committee is expected to give its recommendations, including reducing the R&D tax concession from 150 per cent to 125 per cent, to the Senate today. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Coles Myer has shown its A$2.8 million man, Peter Bartels, the door, yesterday announcing he would be cutting short his contract with Australia's largest retailer by six months after a turbulent four-and-a-half years as chief executive. Bartels is to be replaced by his former lieutenant Dennis Eck. Page 25.

After Alan Bond pleaded guilty last week to two fraud charges relating to the stripping of more than A$1 billion from former Bond Corp associate Bell Resources, the Australian Federal Police have continued investigations into possible bankruptcy offences by Bond by seizing documents from the liquidator of the jailed businessman's private company, Dallhold Investments. Page 25.

According to the Boardroom Report, a national survey of Australian company directors released quarterly by the Australian Institute of Company Directors and KPMG, almost three quarters of company directors are expecting a fall in interest rates early nextyear but, in the short term, their outlook for the economy is gloomy. Page 27.

After signing a deal to form a consortium with TNT to operate rail freight services between major Australian centres, effective immediately, Toll Holdings is preparing to move a major portion of its A$80 million a year rail freight business away from National Rail Corporation. Page 27.

Singleton Group managing director Russell Tate said yesterday the A$59.15 million profit from the sale of its five per cent interest in the Ten Group will see the advertising company Singleton pay out a special dividend of about A$1.80-a-share to its sharholders in July and dramatically expand its marketing activities. Page 27.

Despite the official integration of Challenge Bank's Victorian assets, Bank of Melbourne managing director David Airey said the bank, which is now the State's fourth largest bank with a 16.6 per cent share of retail lending and a 11.1 per cent share of retail deposits, expected a steady December half-year, in line with internal expectations. Page 27.
THE AGE

Analysts believe the appointment of Dennis Eck as Coles Myer's new chief executive will help turn the retail group around after it recorded a 34 per cent drop in profit in 1995-96 and a traumatic year after the Yannon transaction revelations. Peter Bartels will step aside for Eck on December 31. Page C1.

Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer is expected to protest strongly to the Japanese at the World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore this week over concerns that Japan is violating the spirit of the GATT trade treaty by dumping Australian rice in the form of aid to poor countries. Page C1.

According to the World Trade Organisation's annual report released yesterday, Australia's total share of world trade has dropped to its lowest point ever, despite increases in its market share in almost every key area of world trade in the 1990s. The results reflect the decline in the importance of commodity exports and the trend for Western countries to surrender some of their excess market share to rising Asian countries. Page C1.

Continuing its long-running investigation of jailed businessman Alan Bond for possible breaches of the Bankruptcy Act, the Australian Federal Police has seized documents from the liquidator of Bond's private company, Dallhold Investments. Codenamed Operation Oxide, the investigation is also looking into whether Bond perjured himself in breach of the Commonwealth Crimes Act. Page C1.

Toll Holdings and TNT have signed an agreement to form a consortium to operate rail freight services between major Australian centres. Toll managing director Paul Little said by March a significant percentage of the company's volume might be moving on TN's trains, when TNT acquires extra capacity after the sale of Australian National rolling stock. Page C3.

Qantas Airways Ltd announced yesterday that passenger growth for September was 6.3 per cent for the core airline and 5.8 per cent for the group. The airline also recorded similar growth in revenue passenger kilometres and available seat kilometres to record trong seat factors of 73.1 per cent for the core airline and 72.9 per cent for the group. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
